description:
Vital Recorder is open on the Windows desktop. Three real intraoperative vital signs recordings from the VitalDB open dataset are available in C:\Users\Docker\Desktop\VitalRecorderData\: 0001.vital, 0002.vital, and 0003.vital. Each recording contains intraoperative event markers placed by the anesthesia team (e.g., 'Case started', 'Surgery started', 'Surgery finished', 'Case finished').

You are a perioperative medicine researcher building a surgical workflow database. Your task is to extract and structure the complete event timeline from all three case recordings.

You must:
1. Open each of the three recordings in Vital Recorder and review the event markers listed in each file.
2. Export each case's full vital signs data to a separate CSV file on the Desktop: case_0001_events.csv, case_0002_events.csv, and case_0003_events.csv.
3. Produce a structured event timeline database saved as C:\Users\Docker\Desktop\event_timeline_db.txt. This document must list every event from every case in a tabular format. For each event, record: the Case_ID, the Event_Name, the time elapsed in minutes from the start of that case (Time_from_Start_min), and the perioperative Phase (pre-operative, intraoperative, or post-operative). Use clear column headers and include all events from all three cases.

The event database must be comprehensive — include events from all three cases and categorize them correctly by perioperative phase.

Login: Windows Desktop user (no Vital Recorder login required). Data files are in C:\Users\Docker\Desktop\VitalRecorderData\.
